children: ) auction on Wednesday met with lackluster demand, with market participants demanding the highest yield since 2006.

The notes cleared at a yield of 5.033%, approaching the 5.203% high seen eighteen years ago. Investors required a large premium to absorb the debt, demanding a return more than three basis points above the expected 5.002% rate heading into the bidding deadline, Bloomberg reported.

This steep concession made it the second-weakest five-year auction since 2018, Bloomberg noted, outperforming only the June 2022 sale that immediately followed a massive 75-basis-point Federal Reserve rate hike.
Appetite for the newly issued debt was noticeably soft. The bid-to-cover ratio slipped to 2.21, down from the recent six-month average of 2.33.
The sluggish auction results, combined with strong underlying economic data, accelerated a broader retreat in U.S. government debt, with
surging to nearly two-decade highs. Rates on the five-year tenor exceeded 5% for the first time since 2007.

title: U.S. 5-year Treasury note auction pays highest yield since 2006
